Definition: feminine of G2563; a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble:--stubble.
BiblicalUsage: Kalame is stubble — the stalk of grain left after the harvest, the lightest and least of building materials. Paul says if any man build on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble, the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that stubble is the test of my building: what is light and dry will burn, and only what is precious survives the fire.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
